title: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B on Strata: decode speed
additional_information:
# Objective

Maximize decode throughput (decode_tps) for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on the Strata engine, on the fixed workload below, without losing text quality or exceeding the memory guard.

This campaign is a hill climb: every candidate is built from source and measured by the judge; only a confirmed win becomes the new champion.

# Fixed workload and environment

- Rig: windows-rig, RTX 3070 8 GB, 26 GB RAM, WSL2 Ubuntu, CUDA 12.6, sm_86.
- Engine: Strata, built from this project with `build_kit.sh` (cmake + ninja). The Qwen3.6 path is `src/qwen35/`; `q36_engine.cu` is the main file.
- Model: `llmfan46/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-uncensored-heretic-Native-MTP-Preserved-Q5_K_S.gguf` at `/models/qwen36-heretic/`, architecture `qwen35moe`, 41 blocks (40 trunk + 1 MTP), 2048 embedding, 512 FF, 2 KV heads, head_dim 256. The MTP block is present and drafting works.
- Cells measured: `ctx0` (prompt 1 token) and `ctx32k` (prompt 32768 tokens). Both use output 2048, concurrency 1, greedy. 64K and 128K are NOT measured here: with fp32 K/V (45,056 B/token) a 64K cache is 2.82 GiB and cannot start beside the model. That is a separate campaign's job.
- Baseline on record: 21.6 tok/s decode at ctx0, peak 7.26 GiB VRAM, prompt chunk 1024, server context 36864. The judge measures the seed again as the baseline; treat 21.6 as the number to beat.

# What may change

The engine, its build and its serving flags are the candidate. `src/`, `include/`, `serve/`, `serve.sh`, `cmake/`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `build_kit.sh`, `apps/` and `third_party/` are editable. You may rewrite kernels, add CUDA launches, change quantization handling, thread placement, graph capture and option parsing.

What must not change: the model file, the tokenizer, the sampling settings, the prompt format, the output length, the concurrency, the benchmark client, the kit, or the kit's run wrapper. fp32 K/V must stay the default path; a quantised cache must be opt-in behind a flag.

# Guards

- Peak VRAM per GPU must stay below 7.9 GiB (the kit fails a run above it). The card has 8 GiB; do not plan on more.
- Greedy text on the parity prompts must keep match_rate >= 0.95 against the champion (the kit fails below it). A change that produces plausible but different text is a correctness bug, not a speed win.
- A context that does not fit must fail loudly. Never run with a truncated cache.

# Prior local measurements to steer by (not this tree)

Another agent ran exploratory builds on this same rig and model family. These are direction, not a base commit, and some came from a Q4_K file that this campaign cannot use (a different quant changes the text and fails match_rate):

- Raising expert slots helped: 50 slots gave empty-context 45.8 tok/s; ~55 slots was the safe next step, with decode-time scratch already peaking 7.67 GiB at 50.
- `CPU_THREADS=8` beat the pool default: 48.1 tok/s empty (+4.9%).
- `MTP=2` beat `MTP=3` (42.3 vs 45.8 empty).
- With MMQ on, prompt prefill was ~153 tok/s; freeing MMQ's staging for more slots dropped prefill to ~89 tok/s. MMQ is worth keeping for prompts; the trade must be measured, not assumed.
- Q4_K raised empty-context throughput by about 21%, but that is a different weights file and out of scope here.

So the promising axes on THIS tree are: expert placement and slot count, CPU threads, MTP drafts, prompt chunk, KV precision, MMQ/kernel switches, CUDA graph and launch overhead.

# Queue of ideas (starting points, not rules)

1. Expert placement: sweep `--expert-vram`, `--expert-slots`, `--hybrid-rows` to keep more experts resident and cut paging. Measure peak VRAM at ctx0 and ctx32k; stop before the guard.
2. CPU threads and affinity: sweep `CPU_THREADS` 0/6/8/10 and pool affinity for the expert GEMMs.
3. Drafting: sweep `--mtp` 0..4 and `--batch-mtp`; keep MTP=2 as the reference.
4. Prompt chunk: sweep `PREFILL` 512/1024/2048 and `STRATA_Q36_CHUNK` / `STRATA_Q36_READ_WINDOWS`; report prefill_tps and ttft_ms as info.
5. Quantised K/V in `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`: add `--kv fp32|f16|int8|int4` with fp32 default. int4 makes 64K 0.35 GiB and frees VRAM for more experts and a bigger chunk. Stage f16, then int8, then int4, and prove each with `STRATA_Q36_VERIFY=1` and the parity gates.
6. Kernel switches: MMQ / V2K / Q8_PACKED paths, fused QK-norm-rope, anything that cuts a launch or a read.
7. CUDA graphs: capture the decode step for the shapes used; reduce per-token launch overhead.
8. KV layout: group size, scale dtype, hot rows kept in fp32, fused dequant into attention.

# How to judge a change

Report decode_tps for ctx0 and ctx32k, prefill_tps, ttft_ms, peak VRAM and match_rate. A win is a change that raises the primary metric beyond the 2% minimum effect on at least one cell without breaking a guard on either cell. Prefer changes that help both cells.

# Definition of done

The campaign keeps climbing until the wall-time budget is spent or the owner pauses it. Keep the champion buildable and honest: a candidate that only wins by skipping work, changing the workload, or weakening a guard is not a win.
ideas: Expert placement and slot count: sweep --expert-vram, --expert-slots, --hybrid-rows; ~55 slots was safe at 7.67 GiB in an earlier local experiment
CPU threads and pool affinity: sweep CPU_THREADS 0/6/8/10; 8 won by 4.9% empty in an earlier local experiment
Drafting: sweep --mtp 0..4 and --batch-mtp; MTP=2 beat MTP=3 earlier
Prompt chunk: PREFILL 512/1024/2048, STRATA_Q36_CHUNK, STRATA_Q36_READ_WINDOWS; watch prefill_tps and ttft_ms
Quantised K/V in src/qwen35: --kv fp16|int8|int4, fp32 default, staged and parity-proven
MMQ / V2K / Q8_PACKED kernel switches and fused QK-norm-rope
CUDA graph capture for the decode shape; per-token launch overhead
KV layout: group size, scale dtype, hot rows in fp32, dequant fused into attention
